DHL has multiple ways to ensure that Prohibited Goods are identified. First, we have our CAiA system stored with all the deswcriptions related to the prohibited Goods. Once shipment arrive physically, our GTW staff will then examn the shipment through X-Ray.With any concern or found any shipment suspicious GTW manager, Security and CBSA will be informed. Envio OUT: están controlados por DPA y requieren secuencia de ckpts especificas. Envíos IN: -DOX Son verificados y analizados por Aduanas quienes autorizan el release. -NON DOC 75% de envíos arribados quedan retenidos con intervencion obligatoria del broker. El 25% restante es fisicamente verificado por DNA previo a liberación, por lo que cualquier envio qeu se haya autorizado su liberacion siempre es responsabilildad y autorizado por la DNA. En caso de detectarse envíos mal liberados Aduanas solicita apoyo a DHL, de forma solidaria, para el reingreso de los mismos y subsanar el error

Updated facility authorization is only required when a facility is moved or physically modified. The primary points of the approval that must be kept up-to-date are the employee list and bonded inventory. A new employee list must be submitted to CBP anytime there is a change. The previous list should be compared to current management roster. Inventory is not required to be submitted to CBP, but a physical inventory should be reconciled against open in-bonds sent to that facility. (19 CFR 19.2 and 122.50) Gateways would also require a similar inventory validation. Gateway employee reporting is expanded to include a quarterly report of all employees with access to the secure area. (19 CFR 122.184)

Is there a Country Customs Compliance Lead (CCCL), endorsed by the Country Senior Management Team (SMT)?
Does the CCCL have at least one (1) Individual Key Objective (IKO) related to Customs Compliance?
Are the local procedures documented and up-to-date (as outlined on Annex 1 of the Policy), to ensure compliance with Customs Regulations?
Are there internal awareness communications (regarding Customs Compliance) developed & released internally on a periodic basis?
Are changes in Customs Regulations timely identified, communicated, and implemented operationally?
Are the opportunities/ areas of improvement identified during the last Country Self-Assessment documented on a Country Action Plan (with clear responsibilities & timelines)?
Have the relevant DHL Express Customs personnel received a Country-Specific Customs Operational & Customs Regulatory Training, with a training log created and monitored regularly?
Are Fines & Penalties (or Customs Debt) received from Customs Authorities recorded, monitored & managed locally, including updates in relevant DHL Financial Systems?
Are there Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans in place to reduce / mitigate / avoid recurrent systemic issues identified (which led to Fines & Penalties or Customs Debt)?

Are Fines & Penalties (or Customs Debt) with a value equal or above €10,000 EUR for a single incident (or with a value equal or above €50,000 EUR for a number of incidents of one type within a year) periodically reported to the RCCH (minimum monthly)?

Are Fines & Penalties (or Customs Debt) with a value equal or above €100,000 EUR against DHL Express in connection with a single incident or repeated incidents within a year (and/or violations representing a potential or imminent suspension or removal of a Customs privilege, license, or DHL Express ability to perform Customs services in a country) immediately escalated to the RCCH?
Are potential Voluntary Disclosures pre-aligned and signed-off by the Country Senior Management Team (SMT), GBS Legal, and the CCCL prior submission to Customs Authorities?
Are there Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans in place to reduce / mitigate / avoid recurrent of systemic issues (which led to the Voluntary Disclosure)?

Are payments related to Voluntary Disclosures with a value equal or above €10,000 EUR for a single disclosure (or with a value equal or above €50,000 EUR for a number of disclosures of one type within a year) periodically reported to the RCCH (minimum monthly)?

Are payments related to Voluntary Disclosures with value equal or above €100,000 EUR in connection with a single voluntary disclosure or repeated disclosures within a year (and/or disclosures that may result in a potential or imminent suspension or removal of a Customs privilege, license, or DHL Express ability to perform Customs services in a country) immediately escalated to the RCCH and requested sign-off (pre-approval prior the Voluntary Disclosure)?
Are communications with Customs & Other Government Authorities done in a professionally, accurately & timely manner, approved by DHL stakeholders outlined in the Policy, followed-up & archived?
Are inquiries, requests, issues or investigations regarding compliance with Customs Regulations that may affect the DHL Express’ ability to operate escalated internally (as per the Policy)?

Are Audits and In-Person Visits (planned or unannounced) conducted by Customs & Other Government Authorities immediately notified to relevant parties (as per the Policy), documented with clear meeting minutes /meeting report and follow-up actions agreed?
Has DHL Express obtained the AEO – or equivalent – certification, and maintains the certification status?
Are changes in the AEO – or equivalent – certification status (or if certification is at risk) notified to the RCCH?
Are the Licenses & Permits to operate reviewed on a periodic basis (minimum once a year) to ensure that DHL Express complies with the conditions/requirements stated in a license or permit?
Are the requirements outlined in the country bonded facility authorization reviewed on a periodic basis (minimum once a year) to ensure that DHL Express complies with the conditions/requirements?
Is there a reconciliation inventory control in place, including inventory reconciliation performed at least twice per week (with action plan in case of systemic issues identified)?

Are there controls in place to ensure that Customs systems developments /changes are not creating compliance issues (including controls in case of automations in place, e.g., RPA/Robotic Process Automation)?

Is there a system documentation (including controls in case of automations in place, e.g., RPA/Robotic Process Automation) and system contingency plan (in case of system malfunction and/or system failure - also agreed with Customs Authorities)?

Are the user access right controls (of the country Customs Systems & Applications) in place and up-to-date? (e.g., access granted only to authorized active DHL users and authorized representative from Customs Authorities)

Do the DHL Express employees performing Customs activities have the required qualification? If a Customs Agent License (individual license per employee) is required by Customs Regulations, are there controls in place to ensure that employees have a valid license in place?

Are the required documents signed, dated and uploaded on the DHL Express Third Party Broker SharePoint (plus broker also logged in the country’s Vendor Master Database/VMD) as outlined in the 'Overview – Due Diligence of Third Party Brokers' process document (as per Policy section 3.5)?

Are Third Party Brokers periodically reviewed (minimum once a year) to ensure that the contractual requirements, operational performance and KPIs are met (including transactional-level audits of Customs Declarations)?
Are import/export/transit customs clearance records retained in an orderly and accessible manner for a minimum of five (5) years, or in accordance with regulations (whichever is longer)?

If allowed (as per Customs Regulations), are Pre-Arrival Customs Declarations processed and timely submitted to Customs Authorities prior to physical arrival of shipments, with complete and accurate information as per Customs Regulations requirements? - including (but not limited to) Incoterms®, Customs Value, Tariff Classification, Country of Origin, etc.
Are Manifests timely transmitted to Customs Authorities with complete and accurate information as per Customs Regulations requirements?
Are import shipments compliantly allocated into the correct De Minimis / Low Value / High Value categorization (as per the Customs Regulations requirements)?

Are Import Customs declarations timely transmitted to Customs Authorities with complete and accurate information as per Customs Regulations requirements? - including (but not limited to) Incoterms®, Customs Value, Tariff Classification, Country of Origin, etc.

Are Import Customs Declarations of high-risk/sensitive goods (such as anti-dumping, high-value goods, and other high-risk profiles defined locally) reviewed by (at least) two (2) qualified employees prior to the submission to Customs Authorities?
Are Corrective and Preventive Action Plans (CAPA) requested in case of systemic non-compliant Undervalued (UV) shipments identified?

Are Broker Handover instructions (obtained from customers to handover shipments to their nominated broker) received by the Customs Operations Team and archived in the applicable DHL system(s) – e.g., Customer Master File?
Are there controls in place to ensure that Prohibited Goods are identified during the Customs Clearance process (and handed over to Customs Authorities)?
Are there controls in place to ensure shipments with Restricted Goods are not released without the licenses /permits required by Regulations?
Are Corrective and Preventive Action Plans (CAPA) requested in case of systemic non-compliant Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) infringement shipments identified?
Are there controls in place to ensure that Transit / Bonded Movement shipments are accurately and timely declared to Customs Authorities?
Are the DHL guarantees (related to Transit / Bonded Movements) in place (as per Customs Regulations), with sufficient coverage?
Are controls in place to ensure compliant Temporary Imports/Exports declarations to Customs Authorities?
Are there controls in place to ensure that Post Clearance Modifications (PCM) are filed, monitored for progress, and followed-up until closure?
Is there a root cause assessment performed for Post Clearance Modifications (PCM) and definition of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans for systemic issues to prevent reoccurrence?
Are there controls in place to ensure that Diplomatic Shipments identified & processed in accordance with Customs Regulations and Global SOP requirements?
Are there controls in place to ensure that Duties & Taxes are paid accurately & timely to Customs Authorities (as per Customs Regulations)?
Are there controls in place to identify and stop Unauthorized Release (URL) shipments from leaving the facility unauthorized?

Is there a root cause assessment performed for systemic issues that led to Unauthorized Releases (URL), and definition of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans for systemic issues to prevent reoccurrence?
Are Export Customs declarations timely transmitted to Customs Authorities with complete and accurate information as per Customs Regulations requirements?

Are Export Customs Declarations of high-risk/sensitive goods (such as high-value goods, and other high-risk profiles defined locally) reviewed by (at least) two (2) qualified employees prior to the submission to Customs Authorities?
Is there a Reconciliation process/report in place to identify discrepancies between the actual physical shipment flow and the data (to ensure compliance with Customs Regulations)?

Is there a root cause assessment performed for systemic issues identified based on the reconciliation discrepancies, and definition of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans for systemic issues identified to prevent repetition of errors?
Is there a Quality Review in place performed for at least 2% of the Formal Export/Import declarations (performed either on a daily or weekly basis)?

Is there a root cause assessment performed based on the systemic issues identified during the Quality Review, and definition of Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans for systemic issues identified to prevent repetition of errors?

Is DHL Express currently acting as IOR/EOR (or sub-contract a Third Party IOR/EOR Service Provider) for DHL own’s Customs purposes if operationally required (as per DHL Express’ own strategic decision) and/or legally required (as per Customs Regulations)? - e.g., for Low Value shipments where Customs Regulations allow.

Are Power of Attorneys (PoA) – or equivalent authorizations - collected from exporters/importers, and archived on the country’s DHL system(s) – e.g., Customer Master File (CMF) - with the respective expiration date (where applicable), as per Customs Regulations requirements?

Are there controls in place to ensure that Material Violations of Customs Regulations or this Policy are reported and investigated (as outlined on the Policy section 6)? NOTE: 'Material Violation' is defined on section 1.6 (Definitions) of the Policy.

Are actual issues (or potential concerns) related to Customs Compliance escalated by the Country Customs Compliance Lead (CCCL) to the Country Senior Management Team (SMT) and to the Regional Customs Compliance Head (RCCH), as outlined in the Policy?

Dado la regulación del pais, los unicos envios que aplican para esta pósibilidad son aquellos que pueden ampararse en la franquicia de compras (producto G) y aquellos que deciden pagar el 60% del valor (producto H) comprendidos en la misma norma de la franquicia. Se adjunta evidencia de los pagos de carga en prearribo liberada en GTW
Se gestiona desde el equipo de GTW y se adjuntan cierres de manifiesto y gestión de Discrepancias via mail

La nueva normativa de Aduanas (lleva 15 dias en practica) habilita el ingreso de cargas hasta USD 800 y 20 kgs de valor sin participación de un broker, pero llevan un tributo unico o podrían estar exentas y se les asigna EnvioTipo G, H o J. Las cargas HV pasan todas por Broker y se asigna EnvíoTipo D

Las transmisiones de Import Formal se hacen a traves de un broker, no las gestiona DHL en sí mismos (N/A). Hasta USD 800 de Invoice Value DDP y 20 kilos sí se declaran directamente bajo el nuevo proceso informal disponible en UY.
Se gestiona desde el equipo de Back TCU y queda registro en Excel de la tabla y de los cambios correspondientes
No contamos con BOND Propio
No brindamos este servicio a través de nuestro Broker Externo
Se sigue instrucciones GSOP y se agrega como evidencia mail de seguimiento del envío (flagging, labelling, etc)
El ejecutivo se asgura de tener el cobro previo al CR y FIN mantiene controles paralelos.

Envio OUT: están controlados por DPA y requieren secuencia de ckpts especificas. Adicional a esto, los envios que no llevan tramite formal (hace el BROKER) son puestos a disposicion de la DNA quienes deciden que sale y que no. Los que no salen son puesto por estos en una jaula. Envíos IN: -DOX Son verificados y analizados por Aduanas quienes autorizan el release. -NON DOC 75% de envíos arribados quedan retenidos con intervencion obligatoria del broker. El 25% restante es fisicamente verificado por DNA previo a liberación, por lo que cualquier envio que se haya autorizado su liberacion es responsabilildad de la DNA. En caso de detectarse envíos mal liberados Aduanas solicita apoyo a DHL, de forma solidaria, para el reingreso de los mismos y subsanar el error. Se adjuntan los ultimos ejemplos

Las exportaciones las gestiona un Broker Externo o en su defecto el propio cliente con su despachante. De nuestro lado se recibe correo específico con el tipo de envío, se maneja en ruta dedicada, y se entrega a TCU EXPO segregado de la carga general en horario específico (Hasta 16 hs)
DHL no gestiona Declaraciones de EXPO, las hace el broker del cliente o nuestro broker asociado
DHL no actúa como EOR/IOR en UY
Los gestiona y registra el Broker Externo
Se conducen inspecciones a todos los envíos que pasan por OUT, Se detectó un caso del ultimo período, se agregan evidencias del proceso.

La comunicación con el Broker Externo es fluída, constante y transparente. Los casos en los que se detectan posibles preocupaciones se revisan asap y se declaran como corresponde con la participación del Gte de OPS quien, llegado el caso, lo eleva a SMT y CM
Se conducen inspecciones a todos los envíos que pasan por OUT, Se detectó un caso del ultimo período, posibles inflamables y error en simulacro SALT

Solo existen requerimientos aduaneros respecto a los sobrantes o faltantes solo a nivel de HAWB que deben ser cumplidos por las compañías aéreas trasportistas.
Mensualmente se realizan auditorías del despachante de la Agencia de Aduanas y las declaraciones aduaneras de envíos Low Value.

En el caso de AR DHLE funciona como IOR/EOR, para la liberación de todos los envíos Low Value Inbound y Outbound. Para la liberación Formal DHLE actúa especificamente como EOR en los casos de utilizar el servicio de Exporta Simple. Sin embargo, no se han encontrado casos donde se ha inciado un pedido o evaluación para actuar como IOR/EOR para clientes específicos. Sólo se ha hecho uso de la figura legal de DHLE como EOR en un caso especial como excepción que se ha subido al iShare

Como parte del plan de mejora, el área definió las siguientes acciones para 2026 – Gestores Gateway (Art. 174): - Presentación de documentación : Es fundamental evitar la entrega de documentos que puedan generar observaciones o dudas durante la revisión por parte del funcionario DHL. - Cumplimiento estricto de requisitos : Se debe asegurar la entrega exacta de la documentación solicitada por Aduanas. No se debe aceptar documentación informal o declaraciones firmadas. Siempre se debe respaldar el proceso con documentos formales, tales como: Factura firmada por el proveedor,Cartolas bancarias, Documentos verificables y trazables - Escalamiento semanal de casos sin resolución : De manera semanal, se deben escalar a la jefatura de Aduana Courier todos los casos (DIPS) que se encuentren pendientes de resolución. - Revisión diaria de guías : Es obligatoria la revisión diaria de todas las guías, sin excepción, con el fin de evitar acumulaciones y retrasos en la operación.

En el caso de Chile, conforme a la normativa aduanera vigente aplicable a los envíos de bajo valor (LVD), DHL se encuentra facultada para efectuar directamente el pago de los derechos, impuestos y gravámenes asociados a dichas operaciones, sin que sea necesaria la confirmación previa del cliente.

Los casos de infracciones materiales a las regulaciones aduaneras o a esta política son debidamente reportados e investigados. En DHL Express Chile, dichas investigaciones se llevan a cabo utilizando las grabaciones de nuestro sistema de circuito cerrado de televisión (CCTV), en coordinación con distintas áreas de la compañía y adaptándose a las necesidades específicas de cada caso.
Se realiza un seguimiento continuo de temas regulatorios para la alta dirección, enfocado en el cumplimiento aduanero.

Se identifica una oportunidad de mejora en la gestión y difusión de los procedimientos operativos, tanto globales como internos de cada área. Actualmente, no se asegura que todos los equipos conozcan adecuadamente estos documentos ni su ubicación, lo que puede derivar en una aplicación inconsistente de los procesos. Asimismo, se observa que los procedimientos no se encuentran completamente integrados ni vinculados a una matriz de conocimiento formal, lo que limita la trazabilidad, el control y la estandarización de la información disponible para los colaboradores.
Análisis de causa raíz + Planes de remediación
Manager, Gateway

Durante las entrevistas aleatorias realizadas a distintos equipos, con diversos niveles de permanencia en la organización, se evidenció que el personal no hace referencia a normas específicas del Compendio de Normas de Aduanas ni a procedimientos internos formalmente publicados. En su lugar, la base de conocimiento se sustenta principalmente en la transmisión informal de información, heredada de otros funcionarios que previamente desempeñaron funciones similares.
4.3 Subvaloración del despacho de importación (UV)

Actualmente, no se cuenta con un enfoque sistemático para el análisis de causa raíz, ni con un uso continuo de reportes orientados al monitoreo de tendencias y a la identificación de oportunidades de mejora. Asimismo, el reporte semanal de UV, que podría constituir una herramienta clave de control y gestión, no se utiliza de manera consistente para el seguimiento de variables críticas, tales como tipo de producto, proveedor y número de cuenta.
4.11 Lieración no autorizada (URL)

Se detectaron salidas irregulares durante el período auditado. En estos casos, se evidencian brechas en los levantamientos internos y en la existencia de procedimientos estandarizados, previamente acordados con el equipo, necesarios para evaluar adecuadamente los riesgos asociados. Esto dificulta la adopción de acciones oportunas y en tiempo real.

Durante el período de enero a mayo de 2026, se han detectado ocho salidas irregulares, lo que podría derivar en sanciones relacionadas con el valor aduanero. Entre estas se contempla la eventual calificación de contrabando conforme al Artículo 168 de la Ordenanza de Aduanas y la resolución Exenta N°718 19.02.2020 anexo D, con un impacto financiero estimado de YTD €2,7K. y un acumulado de €74K. Asimismo, existe la posibilidad de iniciar expedientes disciplinarios, ya sea a nivel grupal o individual, que podrían implicar multas de hasta 25 UTM o la suspensión de actividades por el plazo que determine el Director Nacional de Aduanas.
4.14 Revisiones periódicas de la calidad de las declaraciones de aduanas

Se detectó que los controles de calidad están enfocados principalmente en las destinaciones cursadas por DHL; sin embargo, existen desviaciones en el control del manejo de la información transmitida a la Aduana. En algunos casos, aun cuando no existe una destinación gestionada por DHL, la información no es debidamente validada.

Adicionalmente, se observa que el uso de herramientas automatizadas carece de una inducción adecuada y de controles de capacitación formales, lo que genera reprocesos y riesgos de errores masivos, particularmente en DHUB.

Customs Compliance tendra mesas de trabajo con los Brokers cada que se publiqué un cambio regulatorio que impacte a la Compañía para revisar la forma en la que se plasmarán dichos cambios en los Pedimentos.

En cuanto sean publicados cambios que impacten las operaciones de la Compañía, se llevarán a cabo sesiones con los Agentes Aduanales para alinear la forma en la que se realizarán los pedimentos, siempre dentro de la normatividad aduanera aplicable.

Adicional, el área de verificación de la Agencia Aduanal realiza una revisión de todos los campos en el pedimento antes del pago; así como, cuatro Auditorías al año a los procesos Formal y Global, divididas en dos auditorías internas y dos auditorías externas. Informal: Fines and penalties issued by the Customs Department of the customs authorities are recorded, monitored, and managed, and are also forwarded to the Finance Department so that they can be properly entered into the relevant systems and reported to the Regional team regarding their status. Attached is the follow-up regarding this control, also available at the link: https://app.powerbi.com/links/Z12Z2bOLrz?ctid=cd99fef8-1cd3-4a2a-9bdf-15531181d65e&pbi_source=linkShare Formal: Fines and penalties received by the Customs department from customs authorities are recorded, monitored, and managed, as well as forwarded to the Finance department so that they are properly entered into the relevant systems in that department and reported to the Regional team regarding their status.

Yes. Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans have been implemented to address and mitigate identified systemic issues, with the aim of reducing, mitigating, or preventing recurrences. Over the past 12 months, no systemic issues have been identified that have resulted in fines, penalties, or customs charges.

We conduct a monthly review of fines and penalties, and we have not had any cases involving an amount of €10,000 or more for a single incident (or an amount of €50,000 or more for multiple incidents of the same type within a year); for this reason, no report was filed.
In the past year, we have not received any fines of €100,000 or more

Yes. Potential voluntary disclosures undergo a preliminary review and formal approval before being submitted to customs authorities, involving the Senior Management Team (SMT), the GBS Legal Department, and CCCL, in accordance with applicable internal governance and compliance protocols. During the period under review, there were no instances of voluntary disclosures.

Yes. Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans are in place to address and mitigate systemic issues whenever they are identified, with the aim of preventing recurrence. However, in the past 12 months, no systemic issues have been identified that have resulted in Voluntary Disclosure, and therefore there was no need to activate CAPA plans specifically related to cases of Voluntary Disclosure during that period.
In the past 12 months, we have not had any incidents involving a single disclosure of €10,000 or more (or involving €50,000 or more)
In the past 12 months, we have not had any incidents involving amounts of €100,000 or more.

Yes. All communications with Customs and other government authorities are conducted in a professional, accurate, and timely manner, exclusively through notifications on the e-CAC portal, with a responsible signature. These communications are pre-approved by the relevant parties at DHL in accordance with the Customs Compliance Policy, and are properly tracked and archived to ensure traceability and regulatory compliance.

Yes. All inquiries, requests, issues, or investigations related to compliance with customs regulations that may impact DHL Express’s operations are properly identified and escalated internally, in accordance with the workflows, levels of responsibility, and guidelines set forth in the Customs Compliance Policy.

Yes. All audits and on-site visits (whether scheduled or unscheduled) conducted by Customs and other government authorities are immediately reported to the relevant parties, in accordance with the Customs Compliance Policy. These events are formally documented with clear minutes or reports, agreed-upon follow-up actions, and evidence properly filed in a control system, ensuring traceability and compliance.

Yes, DHL Express has held Cargo Agent and Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) certifications since 2019 and continues to maintain this certification status. https://dpdhl.sharepoint.com/sites/normativa17/OEA/Forms/AllItems.aspx
There are no changes that would jeopardize DHL's AEO certifications.

The legal department drafted a specific contract for these services in accordance with global guidelines and even had the service agreement notarized to ensure transparency and legal certainty for DHL.

Operating licenses and permits are reviewed periodically, at least once a month, to ensure that DHL Express complies with all established conditions and requirements. Due to the rigorous controls in place, no gaps were identified regarding unmet conditions. The regulatory department manages all operating licenses and permits through CRISP and Power Automated.
In addition, the expiration dates for licenses and authorizations have been automated, and we continue to perform manual checks in the most critical cases.

Yes. The requirements set forth in the country’s bonded warehouse authorization are reviewed periodically, at least once a year, through a formal regulatory monitoring process. The purpose of this review is to ensure that DHL Express remains in continuous compliance with all conditions, obligations, and legal requirements applicable to the operation and customs clearance of authorized facilities.

Yes. There is a formal inventory reconciliation process in place that covers both Courier and Formal operations. Reconciliation is performed daily, exceeding the minimum requirement of at least twice a week. In Courier, the reconciliation report is prepared daily, saved in the corporate repository (SharePoint), and forwarded to the support analyst for consolidation and generation of management dashboards in Power BI, enabling continuous monitoring, traceability, and tracking of any discrepancies. In Formal, the reconciliation control includes verification upon shipment arrival, as provided for in the applicable operational procedures, as well as an additional control, which consists of extracting shipment status from the HMS system and comparing this information with the shipments physically stored in the secure area (cage) through physical scanning. The generated reports are properly archived in a specific folder in Teams, ensuring traceability, documentary evidence, and compliance with regulatory requirements for inventory reconciliation. If systemic issues are identified, a corrective action plan is in place to address the root cause and prevent recurrences.
The local IT team conducts audits to ensure compliance. However, not all changes go through the CCCL submission and approval process.

Yes, there is system documentation and a contingency plan for the Connected system. There is a formal BCP (IT-7042) that includes operational controls, recovery procedures, backups, RTO/RPO, and a communication plan, ensuring the continuity of critical processes—including customs obligations—in the event of failures or outages.

Yes. Access controls for Customs Systems and Applications are in place and up to date. Access is granted only to active, authorized DHL users and authorized representatives of Customs Authorities. The Regulatory Affairs team conducts comprehensive annual reviews of access rights, while the Operations teams conduct quarterly reviews, including of the CONNECTED system.

Yes. DHL Express employees who perform customs-related activities in Brazil possess the necessary qualifications, in accordance with local customs regulations and DHL’s internal Operational Instructions, which define job profiles, responsibilities, and mandatory training. Brazilian customs legislation does not require DHL Express employees to hold an individual Customs Broker license with an expiration date. Customs broker credentials are regulated, controlled, and published by the Customs Authority itself (Brazilian Federal Revenue Service). If a customs broker loses their authorization, access to customs systems is automatically blocked, preventing them from performing their duties. Thus, active status confirms the validity of the authorization. DHL Express maintains documentary evidence of appointments and credentials, as well as internal controls aligned with the official mechanisms of the Customs Authority.

Yes. All required due diligence documents (DDQs, SCOC, and contract) are signed, dated, and properly uploaded to the DHL Express Third-Party Forwarders SharePoint site. The Regulatory Affairs team uses an automated workflow in Power Automate to monitor the validity of the documents, ensuring ongoing compliance. Control is currently performed through the DDQ, with a transition to the Shield tool underway in 2026. All freight forwarders are also registered in the country’s Vendor Master Database (VMD).

Yes, third-party customs brokers are reviewed periodically, with formal performance evaluations conducted at least once a year, in addition to quarterly performance reviews. These reviews assess contractual compliance, operational performance, SLAs, and KPIs, as defined in the contract. Additionally, Quality Reviews include transaction-level audits of Customs Declarations, ensuring accuracy, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.

Yes. Customs clearance records for imports, exports, and transit are maintained in an organized, traceable, and accessible manner for a minimum period of 5 years, or as required by applicable regulations.
Formal Import: Documentation is stored digitally in the corporate system (iShare), with access controls. The original documents accompany the shipment for the customer’s safekeeping; when not picked up, they remain physically stored in controlled areas (airport or storage provider).
Formal Export: Archiving is fully digital, with documents available in official and corporate systems (Portal Único/RFB, Connected, GIA/Sherloc).
Informal: ANVISA and MAPA documents remain archived at MCT for an indefinite period exceeding 5 years, and RFB release records are stored on the Portal Único.
Spot checks are conducted as required, with documented evidence available in the retention systems.

For informal import operations, when permitted by Brazilian customs legislation, pre-arrival customs declarations are processed promptly and in accordance with regulatory requirements. The data is fully cleaned, validated, and entered into the local application (Connected), including all mandatory information for the customs declaration, such as Incoterms®, customs value, tariff classification, and country of origin. After validation, and within the regulatory deadline (up to 4 hours before the flight’s arrival in Brazil), a formal notification is sent to the GTW department to proceed with the operational steps. As evidence, the daily log of processed flights, with their respective details, is attached. For Formal Imports, it is clarified that Pre-Arrival Customs Declarations are neither provided for nor practiced in Brazil.

Yes. Informal: Manifests are submitted to Customs Authorities in a timely manner, on average 2 hours prior to the flight’s arrival, containing complete and accurate information for all shipments (e.g., medications, duty-free items). The process is carried out in coordination with the Locate team, with system-based recording and reporting to the Federal Revenue Service.
Formal: Manifests are transmitted in advance to Customs Authorities in accordance with Customs Regulations, containing complete and accurate information. Transmission is handled by the Aviation team, based outside Brazil, in coordination with the airline, with transmission records and controls maintained by that team.

Yes. Formal: Any discrepancies identified in the manifest are recorded, tracked, and addressed by the team responsible for transmitting the manifest (Aviation), which notifies the relevant parties and Customs Authorities, when applicable, in accordance with regulatory requirements.
Informal: Identified discrepancies are duly recorded in a specific report and submitted to Customs Authorities whenever required by regulation or upon request.

Formal: The allocation of Formal Import shipments does not follow this categorization, as is the case with Courier Imports. For Formal Imports, there is no value limit; rather, the importer chooses this method.
Informal: There is a value limit for importing as Informal (courier), up to USD 3,000.00 for Brazil. For Formal imports, the value is unlimited.

Formal: Import customs declarations are submitted to customs authorities with complete and accurate information, which is verified with the importing customer. However, unlike the process for Courier Imports, Formal clearance does not have a strict deadline for clearance registration. The respective declaration is made once by mutual agreement between the importer and their own customs broker, or the DHL customs broker (when the customer chooses DHL as the customs broker), and only after the cargo has been properly received by the airport operator.
Informal: Yes. Import customs declarations are transmitted in a timely manner as soon as the flight is made available in the system by Locate for entry into Siscomex. In addition, the manifest is sent as required, at least 2 hours prior to the aircraft’s arrival, in full compliance with customs regulations.

Informal: Courier shipments classified as high-risk/sensitive are those with a value exceeding USD 3,000.00, as specified in the attached procedure. Shipments exceeding USD 3,000.00 that arrive via courier are returned to the last point of entry to re-enter Brazil under the Formal procedure, in accordance with local legislation.
Formal: Regarding the review of Customs Declarations considered high-risk, it was agreed between the business unit (Customs) and the Regulatory team that the Customs team will handle reviews for shipments starting at USD 70,000. The respective review is handled by at least two analysts, followed by the direct manager. The Full Analyst enters the process data, which is forwarded to the Senior Analyst, who in turn analyzes, validates, and forwards it to the Supervisor for final review, authorizing the declaration’s registration. The link below contains all approvals made since the start of this review in 2025. https://dpdhl.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/aduanasdesembaraco/EXhLu7nasA9KvaqSNzVut-4Bg91mgqHYSmE1SdNYseVSJQ?email=Danilo. Borges%40dhl.com&e=czJ9uF - https://dpdhl.sharepoint.com/teams/ AduanasFormal/Shared%20Documents/Forms/AllItems.aspx?id=%2Fteams%2FAduanasFormal%2FShared%20Documents%2FGeneral%2FIMPORT%20DOCUMENTS&p=true&ga=1
We have not experienced any systemic issues related to undervalued shipments over the past 12 months.

Regarding Formal Import shipments released at our Formal warehouse, the shipment is not delivered to a designated customs broker, since, once it is at the DHL warehouse, the release will be handled by a DHL customs broker. After release, the shipment automatically enters our domestic network for final delivery. When the shipment is located in a warehouse other than DHL’s, with the importer’s own customs broker, the instruction/authorization to deliver the shipment to the designated customs broker must be sent directly by the importing customer to that other warehouse; DHL does not intervene at this stage. Therefore, these instructions are not filed.

Informal: Yes, there are controls in place to ensure that prohibited goods are identified during the customs clearance process. This is achieved through document verification by the clearance team and physical inspection using X-ray scanning. The Held return team also conducts an analysis based on the description of the contents in the packing list.
Formal: For IMP Formal shipments to be released at our warehouse, the identification of the goods and their classification as restricted/prohibited is performed prior to processing the shipment for our warehouse, through analysis of the Customs Clearance Instruction form, completed by the customer, which contains all product descriptions. Given this preliminary analysis, shipments of goods restricted/prohibited by our network do not enter our warehouse. Attached is an example of a Clearance Instruction for a case that was denied because it involved a restricted/prohibited product in IMP Formal (used product).

Formal: When we handle the clearance of a shipment as customs brokers appointed by the client, we conduct a preliminary review of the goods and their tariff classification as indicated by the client. It is during this preliminary analysis that we identify any licenses/authorizations required by regulations. This analysis is conducted after the client completes the Clearance Instructions form and ensures that the release process is carried out in accordance with the customs regulations applicable to the respective contents.

Informal: In the case of shipments containing prohibited items, the team is trained to identify them and, within the system itself (connected), apply a flag prohibiting the entry of this shipment into Brazil and instructing the network to proceed with the return to the origin.

Our current controls, which ensure the accuracy of transit/customs movement declarations, involve daily follow-up with the relevant suppliers and customers to ensure that all documentation related to these transit shipments is in exact order. Attached is a sample of follow-up for more than 20 examples of waybills in transit, regarding consolidated transit movements by the Master, as well as the follow-up/control for a single transit movement for a shipment. Accountability regarding the registration of customs transit declarations and their compliance is a matter between the respective service provider (accredited for this purpose) and the Federal Revenue Service.
Regarding the timely filing of the declaration, this requirement does not apply, since for the shipments referred to here (Formal IMP shipments) there is no deadline for filing the declaration. Registration is only performed once the accuracy of the validated documentation has been confirmed. Attached is the Operational Instruction regarding the flow of Formal IMP DTAs, which addresses individual shipments.
The guarantees are in effect in accordance with the regulations. Insurance coverage provided by the removal service provider.
We don`t work with temporary imports/exports

Yes, we maintain a record saved in SharePoint of all processes we correct after filing. In this record, we include details such as shipment number, filing date, reported error, process stage, and other relevant information. The team accesses this report daily so they can monitor each case individually and ensure no process falls behind. Attached is a screenshot of the spreadsheet/log and the path in SharePoint. Regarding the tracking of post-clearance corrections, all requests made by the tax team after shipments are released are consolidated in the attached spreadsheet. Based on this, we submit the request to the tax inspector, asking for authorization to make the correction. If the request is denied, we respond to the tax team via email, informing them of the denial by the tax authority. When the correction is authorized, we proceed with it, also paying any additional taxes and fines, if necessary. I monitor the entire process until the shipment is effectively cleared in Siscomex. Upon completion, we send the corrected DIR to the tax team.

Post-filing changes (amendments) are evaluated on a case-by-case basis to identify the root cause and ensure that the same error does not recur. However, most errors occur due to a lack of information provided by the client at the time of filing or are requested by the Internal Revenue Service. Whenever we identify errors in tax returns resulting from systemic errors, we seek to analyze the case and identify the root cause. Once it is evident that it is a systemic error, we proceed by opening tickets so that the error can be addressed, identified, and mitigated to prevent recurrence.

Yes. There are controls in place to ensure that diplomatic consignments are properly identified and processed in accordance with customs regulations and global requirements. Diplomatic suitcases are classified in the Connected system with the specific treatment and, from there, receive the OCNT lock to ensure correct release. Evidence of this control is attached, containing a record of 10 consignments processed.

There is an employee who works with the tax team and, using the tools available in Connected, checks all the taxes and duties so that they can certify that there are no outstanding taxes. This process is called '811 Discrepancy Control' and is carried out between the operational and financial teams.

Yes. There are formal controls in place, through systematic audits using the Siscomex system and Connected, to identify and prevent Unauthorized Release (URL) shipments from leaving the facility without authorization. All exceptions are dealt with by immediate blocking, communication to the manager and registration in an official directory, in accordance with the established procedure.

We analyze the root cause of the problem so that it doesn't happen again. In addition, there is a daily audit to check that all shipments that have left GTW have actually been released, if there are any unreleased shipments the hub is notified and the shipment has an ST intercept applied, to return to GTW, no CAPA has been opened, because there has been no systemic error in the last 12 months.

Informal Exports: Yes, all DRE transmissions are made in good time, sent to RFB auditors between 4-5 hours before the flight departs, guaranteeing that clearance is received within the operational deadline. Formal Export: In the Formal Export process, consignments are subject to evaluation and cargo presence by the customs agency, after the procedures have been completed and the relevant documents issued. To ensure compliance and operational control, there is a systemic lock that prevents the physical movement of the shipment before all the mandatory steps have been completed. This lock is linked to the issuing of the physical label, which is necessary for the identification and movement of the cargo. The system only allows the label to be printed once the process has been completed, ensuring that no shipment is moved before it has been duly authorized.

Yes. Export Customs Declarations (DUE) for goods valued at over USD 70,000 must be reviewed by two qualified employees—a Senior Analyst and a Supervisor—before being submitted to Customs Authorities. The system blocks automatic submission, requiring two-level approval to ensure control and compliance. Attached is a step-by-step guide on how this process is carried out.

Informal: Before shipping the import shipments processed that day, all declared shipments listed in the APQ are cross-checked against Siscomex data and verified to ensure they have been cleared by the Federal Revenue Service.
Formal: We maintain daily control over shipments that are systematically manifested to our warehouse, comparing them with those arriving at the respective physical location. The documentation for these shipments is printed so that a physical reconciliation can be performed upon arrival. After this verification, the Warehouse team sends the validation of this reconciliation to the shipment release team, with Customs Management copied. Our reconciliation, through this practice, has always been 100% effective. Attached is the control report, which contains all shipments from this year that entered our facility.

Informal: Yes, we have notified the shipper so that the necessary preventive and corrective actions can be taken. In addition, we have a SharePoint site at VCP where we log issues and the root causes that have been addressed to prevent errors from recurring; however, there have been no systemic issues requiring the opening of a CAPA in the last 12 months.
Formal: In order to ensure proper reconciliation between transmitted system data and the physical characteristics of the shipment, it is important to note that the release process for a Formal Import shipment can only begin once the shipment has been physically received in the Revenue Service’s system. Regarding data accuracy and discrepancies, we closely monitor shipments by comparing the weight measured in our network with the weight measured upon arrival in Brazil. I have attached an example of this control. Regarding other information (import data, freight, etc.), we have another control mechanism, also attached, in place with the responsible team, which details performance and areas for improvement; there have been no systemic issues for CAPA in the last 12 months.
Quality reviews are conducted, during which formal import and export declarations are examined.
